helpCenter.multiDevice.headline: Multi-device: every device is a Bakabase server
helpCenter.multiDevice.intro: Multi-device is how Bakabase runs on every device on your network at the same time. Each computer runs the desktop app, which includes its own server; a NAS runs the server in Docker. Every device keeps its own storage and its own library, and they can all reach each other: see every device's resources from the computer you sit at, or switch the window to another device and manage it as if you were in front of it.
helpCenter.multiDevice.diagram.title: Three Bakabase servers on one local network, each with its own storage
helpCenter.multiDevice.diagram.caption.d: Keeps the movies on its own disks. From its window you can browse the laptop's and the NAS's libraries, or switch over and manage either of them.
helpCenter.multiDevice.diagram.caption.l: Keeps the comics on its own disk. It can do everything the desktop PC can: every computer is an equal, not a client of another.
helpCenter.multiDevice.diagram.caption.n: Keeps the music. It has no screen, so nobody sits at it: the computers browse its library and switch to it to manage it.
helpCenter.multiDevice.diagram.hint: Select a device to highlight its connections.
helpCenter.multiDevice.pillar.title: What every device has
helpCenter.multiDevice.pillar.server.des: The desktop app includes a complete Bakabase server; a NAS runs the same server in Docker.
helpCenter.multiDevice.pillar.storage.de: Each device keeps its own disks and its own library. Resources and their values are never copied between devices; only the definitions you choose to sync are kept the same.
helpCenter.multiDevice.pillar.reach.desc: On the same network, a computer can browse the libraries shared with it and manage the devices that allow it.
helpCenter.multiDevice.ways.title: Two ways to use another device
helpCenter.multiDevice.ways.browse.title: Browse together
helpCenter.multiDevice.ways.browse.desc: Search and view the libraries of all your devices together, in your own window. Read-only: previews and playback happen on your computer.
helpCenter.multiDevice.ways.switch.title: Switch devices
helpCenter.multiDevice.ways.switch.desc: Show another device's own interface in your window and manage it fully (settings, files and tasks) as if you sat in front of it.
helpCenter.multiDevice.ways.switch.where: Left menu → the device switcher at the top
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.title: Side by side
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.see.brows: Resources from all devices, merged, in this computer's interface
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.see.switc: One device at a time, in that device's own interface
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.do.browse: Search, view details, preview and play; nothing changes on the other device
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.do.switch: Everything: edit and delete resources, change settings, run tasks
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.play.brow: On the computer you sit at
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.play.swit: On the computer you sit at
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.access.br: Read-only sharing: a sharing code or an approval
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.access.sw: Management pairing: a pairing code or an approval, with full control
helpCenter.multiDevice.trust: Nothing connects on its own. Each device decides who may read its library and who may manage it, and can take that back at any time.
helpCenter.multiDevice.map.title: See how your devices connect
helpCenter.multiDevice.map.desc: The Device map (left menu → Multi-device → Device map) draws this computer in the middle and your other devices around it, with a line for every connection: library sharing, and who manages whom. Select a device or a line to see its details and act on it — grant, revoke, switch to it, map its folders. Devices found nearby appear as outlines you can connect to. Data sync lines show which device receives another's definitions.
helpCenter.multiDevice.open.management: Let other devices manage this one
helpCenter.multiDevice.browse.headline: Every device's library in one window
helpCenter.multiDevice.browse.intro: Multi-device library searches this computer and the devices that share with it, and merges the results into one list. Each device still answers for its own resources; nothing is copied here.
helpCenter.multiDevice.browse.mock.capti: “This device” shows only what is on the computer you sit at.
“All enabled devices” adds the laptop's comics and the NAS's music to the same list, each marked with the device it lives on.
helpCenter.multiDevice.browse.card.searc: Match names and file names across the devices you choose. Advanced property filters stay in each device's own library.
Details are read-only. Previews and the player run on this computer and nothing is written back, not even play history. Opening a folder needs a path mapping.
helpCenter.multiDevice.browse.card.cover: A device that is offline is reported as not searched, never silently left out of results that look complete.
helpCenter.multiDevice.browse.boundary: To edit, delete or run tasks on another device's resources, switch to that device instead.
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.headline: Manage another device from your window
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.intro: The desktop app can switch its window to a device it manages (a NAS, or another computer's desktop app) and show that device's own interface. You have full control, exactly as if you sat in front of it, and you can switch back at any time.
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.mock.local: This computer's own library, settings and tasks.
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.mock.remot: {{name}}'s library, settings and tasks. Changes made here happen on {{name}}.
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.mock.capti: The window shows this computer. Pick another device in the list to switch to it.
The window shows {{name}}, and the switcher turns amber to say so. Pick this device at the top of the list to come back.
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.play.title: Playing and opening folders stay on the computer you sit at
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.play.capti: Each device you manage has its own path mappings on this computer, set on the Devices and sharing page. Sign-in windows for third-party sites also open on this computer.
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.card.ownUi: The window shows the interface that device ships with, so it always matches the version it runs.
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.card.contr: A paired computer can do anything on the device it manages. Only pair computers you trust.
If a device runs an older version whose interface has no switcher, use “Switch to” in the tray icon's menu to come back.
Asks the device to revoke this computer, then deletes its key here. The device can also revoke this computer at any time.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.headline: Set it up on the Devices and sharing page
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.intro: Every computer has a Devices and sharing page under Multi-device in its left menu. Access is always granted on the device being accessed, one pair of devices at a time.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.browse.shar: Turn on sharing on the other device
On its Devices and sharing page, choose Enable sharing. The page shows its address and can create a one-time code.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.browse.conn: Under Connect another device, find nearby devices or enter its address. Enter its code, or request access and approve it on the other device.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.browse.both: Keep “Also let the other device read my library” ticked (the default), and each device can read the other once it is approved.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.browse.enab: Browsing turns on by itself once access is granted. Open Multi-device library and search all enabled devices.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.manage.allo: Allow it on the device to be managed
Under Let other devices manage this device, turn it on: remote access with pairing required. You can create a pairing code there too.
Under Devices you manage, enter its address and pairing code. Without a code a request is sent; approve it on the other device and your computer finishes pairing by itself.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.manage.swit: Pick it in the switcher at the top of the left menu, or choose Open in this window.
Add path mappings for it on this computer so its files play and its folders open here.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.unrestricte: A NAS or Docker server starts in Unrestricted mode: anyone on its network can manage it without pairing. Bakabase marks such a device with a warning but never changes its setting for you. Switch to it and, on its Configuration page, change “Access from other devices” under Remote access.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.nas: A NAS or Docker server has no window, and no Devices and sharing page. Turn its sharing on with BAKABASE_FEDERATION_SHARING=true or the federation command inside the container. Its pairing codes and approvals are under Configuration → Remote access in its own interface: open its address in a browser.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.codes: Sharing codes and pairing codes are different: a sharing code only lets a device read a library, a pairing code gives full control. Use each in its own section of the page.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.thinClient: Used Bakabase Client before? It has been removed: the desktop app does its job. The first time the desktop app starts, it brings over the servers Bakabase Client was paired with, keys and path mappings included, so nothing has to be paired again. Run it again any time with Import from Bakabase Client under Devices you manage.
helpCenter.multiDevice.concept.sharing.s: How a device lets others read its library, and nothing more.
helpCenter.multiDevice.concept.sharing.l:
A device shares its library only after sharing is turned on there, and only with devices it authorizes: with a one-time code from it, or by approving a request in its notifications or on its Devices and sharing page.
Access has a direction. Reading the NAS does not let the NAS read you, and it never passes on to a third device. “Also let the other device read my library”, ticked by default when you connect, sets up the way back in the same step, so one approval opens both directions.
Sharing never allows changes: a device you share with can search, view and play, but cannot edit or delete anything.
helpCenter.multiDevice.concept.sharing.e:
On the laptop: Devices and sharing → Enable sharing → Create one-time code.
On the desktop PC: Connect another device → the laptop's address and code, with “Also let the other device read my library” ticked.
Both can now browse each other in Multi-device library.
helpCenter.multiDevice.concept.managemen: Full control of another device, granted on that device.

Managing is a different permission from sharing. A computer paired for management can do everything on the other device: edit and delete resources, change settings, run tasks, the same as sitting in front of it.
It is always granted on the device being managed. Turn on Let other devices manage this device there, then either create a pairing code and enter it on your computer, or send a request from your computer and approve it there.
It works in one direction; to manage each other both ways, pair twice. Stop managing on your computer asks the other device to revoke it and deletes the key. The other device can revoke it at any time under Devices that can manage this one.
Approving a request shows the requesting device's name and address. Make sure it is the computer you expect before you approve.
helpCenter.multiDevice.concept.pathMappi: Where another device's folders are, seen from the computer you sit at.

Playing a file and opening its folder always happen on the computer you sit at, with its own player. When the file lives on another device, this computer needs to know where it can reach the same folder, usually as a network share of the same disk.
Each device has its own mappings on this computer, set on the Devices and sharing page. They are only used on this computer and never move or copy files.
In Multi-device library, previews and the player also work without a mapping because the media is streamed from its device; opening a folder needs one. A device you manage needs mappings for both.

The NAS keeps its music under /volume1/music, and this PC reaches the same folder as \\nas\music. With the mapping /volume1/music → \\nas\music, playing /volume1/music/Live/01.flac opens \\nas\music\Live\01.flac in this PC's player.
helpCenter.multiDevice.concept.remoteAcc: Which other devices a server answers, and what they may do.

Every Bakabase server has a remote-access setting that decides what other devices on the network may do with it. Managing a device needs remote access turned on there; Let other devices manage this device turns it on with pairing required. Read-only sharing uses its own authorizations, but also needs remote access to be on.
A NAS or Docker server starts Unrestricted. Bakabase flags such a device under Devices you manage but never changes another device's setting for you: switch to it and, on its Configuration page, change “Access from other devices” under Remote access.
Only use Unrestricted on a network where you trust every device: anyone who can reach it can delete files and change settings. Never expose Bakabase to the internet with port forwarding.
helpCenter.multiDevice.concept.thinClien: The old remote-control app, replaced by switching devices in the desktop app.

Bakabase Client used to be the way to control a server on another machine. The desktop app now does the same by switching its window to that server, while still running its own server, so Bakabase Client has been removed.
The first time the desktop app starts, it reads the servers Bakabase Client was paired with on this computer, keys and path mappings included, and adds them to Devices you manage, so nothing has to be paired again. Devices already managed here are left as they are, and Bakabase Client's own files are never changed.
Installed the desktop app first, or paired more servers in Bakabase Client afterwards? Use Import from Bakabase Client under Devices you manage to run the import again.
